focus: Anchor the card's own form 'si è messo a ridere' – mettersi a = literally 'put yourself to it', a sudden start; add hook and card quote.
Lead with the flip: cercare alone = look for, cercare di + infinitive = try to – quote 'Cerco di capire'.
Sebbene takes subjunctive even for real facts – 'sebbene sia stato lungo' reports something that actually happened; add that angle, drop the bare formula.
English says 'reproached me FOR not having...', Italian uses di + past infinitive – quote 'di non averla avvisata'.
Fix accents in the tip (qui → lì/là, questo → quello) and keep it anchored to this card's qui → li shift.
'Vanno rispettate' = must be respected – andare + past participle carries obligation; quote the card and drop the 'dovere essere' formula phrasing.
First encounter of stare per: 'Sto per partire' = I'm about to leave – on the verge of; give it a hook and the card quote instead of a fragment.
'Si è lasciato convincere' uses an ACTIVE infinitive where English needs 'be convinced' – lasciarsi + infinitive = let it happen to you; make that the hook.
'Andare a trovare' = go VISIT someone, not 'go find' – lead with the trovare flip and quote 'Sono andato a trovare'.
Drop 'right dislocation' – plain words: pronoun first, noun tagged on after as an afterthought; quote 'L'ho già letto, questo libro'.
'Andavano dicendo' = they went around saying – andare + gerund for ongoing/repeated action; quote the card and use plain words, not 'gerundio'.
'Hanno da fare' = they're busy / have things to do – avere da + infinitive; anchor the idiom, note it is not English 'have to do' obligation.
Anchor 'molto da imparare' – avere + noun + da + infinitive here reads as opportunity, not obligation; quote the card.
The real driver is the different subject: chiedere che + subjunctive when you name who must act ('che tutti fossero presenti') vs chiedere di + infinitive; drop 'polite/formal'.
Second angle on mettersi a: effort/resolve – anchor with the card's 'mi sono messo a studiare seriamente'.
Fix the accent (può) and add the literal hook: può darsi = roughly 'it can give itself' = maybe; può darsi che + subjunctive, quote the card.
Anchor this card: 'È necessario che...partecipino' – impersonal è + adjective + che triggers subjunctive; quote the card instead of the generic rule.
'Sosteneva che fosse impossibile' – the subjunctive marks the reporter's distance from the claim; make that the hook, quote 'fosse'.
Anchor the card: direct 'Sono stanco' → reported 'era stanco' – present backshifts to imperfect; add the card quote.
Fix accents (perché) and say it plainly: reported questions after domandare can take subjunctive – 'non fossi venuto'.
Fix 'verrò' accent and stress that Italian uses the PAST conditional 'sarebbe venuto' where English says plain 'would come'.
Plain words, no 'subordinate clause': in the past, 'as soon as he had finished' becomes 'non appena avesse finito', pairing with 'sarebbe tornato'.
Drop 'topicalization/resumptive pronoun' – plain: front the topic with di, echo it with ne: 'Di soldi, ne ha fin troppi'.
Anchor 'Che Dio ti benedica' – che + subjunctive = 'may...'; plain words, drop 'independent subjunctive/exhortations'.
Plain words: 'Che sia chiaro' = let it be clear – che + subjunctive can issue a directive, not just a wish; drop 'exhortative/independent clauses'.
'Sembra che' + subjunctive – anchor 'abbiano già preso'; seeming = uncertainty, hence subjunctive; plain words, not 'congiuntivo passato'.
